claims.text: High-energy ball milling followed by short-duration, low-temperature SPS will produce a hierarchical microstructure in refractory MPEAs.
The proposed processing route will simultaneously increase room-temperature yield strength and tensile ductility.
Cast or conventionally sintered W-Mo-Ta-Nb-V-like refractory MPEAs have a coarse-grained, single-phase BCC structure.
NbMoTaW- and NbMoTaWV-type refractory MPEAs are brittle at room temperature.
The room-temperature brittleness is caused by limited dislocation mobility and insufficient strain-hardening capacity.
HEBM for 20–40 hours will induce severe plastic deformation and solute segregation.
SPS at 100–150 °C below the onset of recrystallization for 5–10 minutes will preserve ultrafine grains while enabling solute clustering.
Mechanical testing within 24 hours of sintering will prevent significant coarsening before testing.
The treated material will contain ultrafine grains smaller than 1 µm with high dislocation density.
The treated material will contain nanoscale coherent solute-rich clusters formed by non-equilibrium segregation during the short anneal.
The resulting structure will be dual-phase or compositionally graded.
The solute-rich clusters will strengthen the alloy by pinning dislocations through Orowan strengthening.
The solute-rich clusters will serve as sites for dynamic strain aging or solute drag.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations that otherwise cause premature crack initiation.
Suppressing grain growth while retaining coherent clusters will promote continuous strain hardening and break the strength–ductility trade-off.
The treated alloy will have a yield-strength increase greater than 30% relative to the as-cast state.
The treated alloy will have a tensile-ductility increase greater than 50% relative to the as-cast state, potentially increasing elongation from below 5% to above 15%.

Solution annealing at about 1000 °C for one hour followed by water quenching typically produces a coarse-grained, single-phase structure with low dislocation density and limited strain hardening in brittle MPEAs.
Moderate-to-high mixing enthalpy makes solute clustering thermodynamically favorable but kinetically hindered at low temperature.
For extremely high-melting-point systems, SPS may not provide sufficient diffusion for clustering within 5–10 minutes.

contradictions.description: The clusters are described as coherent interfaces that facilitate dislocation transmission, but also as Orowan obstacles. Orowan strengthening ordinarily entails bypass of non-shearable obstacles, so the proposed transmission and bypass mechanisms require clarification.
